root_cause: Since 0.123.5 Dependant.is_coroutine_callable / is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable classified a callable only by its innermost target (inspect.unwrap(call), then strip one partial). An async @wraps wrapper around a sync function was therefore treated as sync, and its coroutine was never awaited ('coroutine' object is not iterable). Two more gaps: a callable instance whose __call__ method is itself decorated was never unwrapped, and a callable that is both a sync generator (inner) and an async generator (wrapper) went down the sync contextmanager path, because _solve_generator tested is_gen_callable first.
best_solution: Add module helpers _impartial(f), which strips nested functools.partial layers, and _unwrapped_call(f) = inspect.unwrap(_impartial(f)). In each of the three flags, test both the outer callable (partial-stripped) and its fully unwrapped target, then do the same for its __call__ (the __call__ of the partial-stripped callable, and the __call__ of the unwrapped one), and return True if any level matches. The rule is 'async at any layer means await it', because an async wrapper around sync code, or a sync wrapper around async code, both give back something awaitable. Keep the default of False for classes. Because a wrapped callable can now be both a gen and an async gen, reorder _solve_generator in utils.py to check is_async_gen_callable before is_gen_callable (asynccontextmanager first).
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_dependency_wrapped.py::test_class_dependency, parametrized over 28 routes, each of which must return 200 with body true. It covers sync noop_wrap and async noop_wrap_async wrappers around: plain functions, gens and async gens; callable instances (wrapped instance, or a decorated __call__ that is sync/async/gen/async-gen); classes; and endpoints themselves. The key cases: a class instance with @noop_wrap async __call__ (the bound __call__ must be unwrapped); @noop_wrap def __call__ that yields, sync or async (same); and @noop_wrap_async over a sync gen, which gives an async-gen wrapper around a sync gen, so the async-gen branch has to win in _solve_generator. No new public API.
locating_signals: The statement says 'functools wraps and partial', 'async, generator, async generator, callable instance', and 'analyze the function but also the wrapper'. grep for inspect.unwrap / partial / isgeneratorfunction finds Dependant._unwrapped_call and the is_*_callable cached properties in fastapi/dependencies/models.py. The statement never names the second location, the gen-vs-async-gen dispatch order in _solve_generator (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py); you only reach it by tracing how the flags are consumed.
our_outcome_summary: Failed on all 4 configs (v4/v6/v7/v8). v6, v7 and v8 each scored 24/28. They walked the partial/__wrapped__ chain of self.call and checked each node and node.__call__, but they never unwrapped the bound __call__ method. That failed class-instance-async-wrapped, class-instance-wrapped-gen and class-instance-async-wrapped-gen. None of them touched utils.py, so wrapped-gen-dependency-async-wrapper (async-gen wrapper around a sync gen) still went through contextmanager and failed. v4 (558s, 47 calls) produced no pytest output at all. Its _is_any_async loop follows current = current.__call__ whenever hasattr(__call__) is true. Each access returns a fresh method-wrapper, so the loop never ends for a non-matching callable, and app construction at import hung until timeout. v4 also left a stray test_async_callable.py at the repo root.
generalizable_lesson: When fixing a type-classification predicate (is async / is generator / is callable), list every indirection layer the input can have: wrapper, wrapped, partial, instance, the instance's __call__, and a decorated __call__. Apply the full normalization at every layer, and write a quick matrix script over those combinations before stopping. Then grep every consumer of the predicates. If two flags can now both be true, the if/elif order where they are used decides the behavior and may need to change, and that consumer can live in another file. Never write a loop over getattr(x, '__call__'): it never reaches a fixed point, so bound it or check identity.
acceptable_alternatives: Any normalization that checks every layer works: the outer callable, each partial.func, each __wrapped__, and the __call__ of every one of those, itself unwrapped through inspect.unwrap on the bound method. It must also reorder async-gen before gen in _solve_generator, or make is_gen_callable return False whenever an async-gen layer exists. The loop has to terminate, for example by using inspect.unwrap plus a bounded __call__ step, not an unbounded __call__ walk.
